evidence: Synthetic and large real-world implicit-feedback datasets; NARF implemented with two representative cross-domain recommendation algorithms; baseline comparisons.
rationale: Dataset comparisons support improved recommendations; identifying implicit-feedback noise as the primary cause of existing algorithms' difficulties lacks reported causal isolation.

evidence: Over 500 pre-trained models; ImageNet and DomainNet streams; three downstream task types and 12 datasets; replay, regularization, representation, and loss-sharpness analyses.
rationale: Broad evaluations support the exploratory title and qualified sequential-learning conclusions; the first-investigation claim concerns the specifically scoped self-supervised streaming-data setting.

evidence: Long-text processing tasks; full-KV-model comparisons; reported use of 50% of typical KV-cache costs.
rationale: Halved cache costs support a substantial difference; broad compatibility and consistent superiority across existing LLMs exceed the unspecified long-text evaluation scope.

evidence: 133,588 human judgments on ImageNet and ObjectNet; viewing-time difficulty; model generalization gaps; prediction-depth, c-score, and adversarial-robustness analyses.
rationale: Human judgments substantiate difficulty patterns in two datasets; conclusions about today's object-recognition datasets extend beyond those evaluated datasets.

evidence: Multiple GANs; matching subnetworks at 67–74% sparsity; discriminator pruning and initialization comparisons; unseen-task transfer; SNGAN, CycleGAN, and prior compression baselines.
rationale: Sparse matching subnetworks across evaluated GAN settings support the title; the priority claim is confined to this specifically defined study category.

evidence: Graph-Laplacian eigendecomposition and functional-calculus feasibility; node classification on varied graphs; negative-depth high-pass filtering; eigengraph augmentation with vanilla GCN.
rationale: Theory and node-classification experiments support revisiting depth; repeatedly calling the learned depth optimal lacks a reported optimality guarantee.

evidence: LLaMA 3.2 1B; seven Harry Potter novels unlearned while related web content remains; reference, utility, PII-regurgitation, and red-teaming comparisons.
rationale: The specified model experiment supports increased PII extraction risk; explaining this as redirection toward memorized adjacent data lacks reported mechanism tests.

evidence: Large/small-model decoding with a shared tokenizer; standalone-large-model cost and performance comparison; reported 3–4× acceleration with reduced performance.
rationale: The descriptive framework title asserts no result. Demonstrated speed-quality tradeoffs do not establish that other inference-acceleration techniques lack tunability.

evidence: Standard zero-shot domain-adaptive segmentation benchmarks; in-house surgical dataset with smoke, blood, and low lighting; effectiveness and generalization evaluations.
rationale: The title describes the proposed modules; reported benchmark and adverse-condition surgical evaluations support the stated effectiveness and generalization claims.

evidence: Vanilla, convolutional, spectral-normalization and stacked GAN comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CelebA; qualitative evaluations and quantitative metrics.
rationale: The title describes the framework. Reported improvements are restricted to named GAN architectures and datasets.

evidence: Two VLMs, five physical trigger objects, two malicious behaviors; 92% success inducing acceleration for a pedestrian holding a red balloon.
rationale: The evaluated physical triggers and acceleration attacks support the possibility of jeopardizing driving. The first claim concerns a narrowly defined attack category.

evidence: Multi-agent costly-information mechanism game; polynomial-time optimal incentive-compatible algorithm; unknown-agent online setting with regret bound of order T to the two-thirds.
rationale: The descriptive title makes no result claim. Optimality, coordination necessity and regret results are presented within the specified mechanism-design game.

evidence: Paired structured and semi-structured tables; SQL, LLM and hybrid comparisons; table-size, join, query-complexity and schema-quality benchmark splits.
rationale: The title describes the controlled study. Reported trade-offs concern the benchmark's varied conditions; the priority claim is narrowly defined.

evidence: Off-policy value evaluation with function approximation; logarithmically increasing restart periods; convergence and polynomial sample-complexity analysis; PER-ETD versus ETD experiments.
rationale: Polynomial efficiency is an evaluative attribute supported by the reported complexity analysis. Convergence and bias-variance claims concern the specified restarted ETD procedure.

evidence: Guided 7B models gain up to 24 GSM8K points; QuestCoT gains up to 6/9/5/7 on GSM8K/SVAMP/ASDiv/MultiArith across smaller models.
rationale: The title's first-step advantage is supported by guided-start interventions and gains across four mathematical benchmarks. All-model wording refers to evaluated models.

evidence: Foreground/background perturbation experiments; background perceptual salience measurements; comparisons with conventionally robust classifiers and adversarial-training approaches.
rationale: The tentative title is supported by salience-preserving attacks and robustness comparisons. Suspiciousness is explicitly modeled through cognitive salience rather than asserted universally.

evidence: Transformers versus LSTMs on noisy sparse parity, majority and random k-juntas; sensitivity-based traps and an additional sensitivity-penalizing loss.
rationale: Observed failures and trap interventions support the title. The concluding claim about boolean-function learning generalizes beyond random juntas despite reported parity and majority successes.

evidence: Online reward-model RL versus offline maximum-likelihood fine-tuning; theoretical and empirical investigation of generation-verification-gap settings.
rationale: Universal convergence to likelihood is not established. The abstract scopes its preferred explanation, but does not report specific support for guaranteed optimal-policy selection and reduced-data causality.

evidence: TD3 and TD3+BC baselines; building-control tasks, weather conditions, deterministic/stochastic scenarios; combined comfort-energy reward improves 40.7% offline and 49.7% online.
rationale: Reported building-control improvements support RUBICON. The motivating explanation that rule-based control underperforms because it cannot ingest many parameters lacks reported causal evidence.

evidence: WikiText-103 automatic and human generation evaluations; token-level autoregressive efficiency comparisons; collection-switch domain adaptation and larger-collection scaling experiments without retraining.
rationale: Copying works in reported generation evaluations, but the unqualified sufficiency title exceeds one named language-modeling benchmark. Abstract results remain tied to described experiments.

evidence: Pre-trained NeRF and Gaussian Splatting models; function-approximation analysis; unspecified evaluations of PH-Dropout.
rationale: Operating on pre-trained models supports practical applicability. The abstract's real-time assertion lacks a reported speed evaluation; generic effectiveness evaluations do not establish runtime.

evidence: Kyber secret-key recovery from power leakage; employed DL-SCA models; CNNC, MDMSD, ZMUV, MMD and ADA comparisons using mean rank and top-k accuracy.
rationale: The title describes cross-device attacks. Any-base-model benefits exceed the employed models on Kyber, and superiority over all recent approaches exceeds the named comparisons.

evidence: SGD versus Adam across batch sizes up to the full dataset; comparisons with simpler SGD variants and sign descent with momentum.
rationale: Full-batch comparisons directly test stochastic-noise explanations. Similarity to momentum sign descent is reported cautiously, supporting the title's tentative alternative explanation.

evidence: English/Chinese benchmarks versus GPT-3, OPT, BLOOM and ERNIE TITAN; INT4 with almost no loss; inference on four RTX3090 or eight RTX2080Ti GPUs.
rationale: The title describes an open bilingual model. Reported inference hardware supports affordability, but most-ever-affordable superiority lacks corresponding hardware-cost comparisons across 100B-scale models.

evidence: Memorization-capacity analysis; gradual versus one-shot pruning; ResNets on CIFAR10/ImageNet; ResNet50 reaches 75.02% top-1 at 80% pruning using 22% of epochs.
rationale: Sooner-is-better conflicts with reported accuracy degradation before weight saturation. The assertion that all prior work requires iterative pruning exceeds the cited examples and experiments.
